questions.q: What is the purpose of source analysis at the start of a migration?
options: To load the data as fast as possible
To decide which Salesforce edition to buy
To profile the source data (row counts, blanks, duplicates, keys) so problems are found before loading
To delete the source system
questions.explain: Profiling the source exposes surprises early, when they are cheap to handle.

questions.q: Why should you decide what NOT to migrate?
options: Stale, duplicate, or junk data adds cost, storage use, and validation work without adding value
Salesforce refuses to store more than 10,000 records
Old records can never be loaded through Data Loader
Omitting data makes the load run without errors automatically
questions.explain: Migrating everything is not a goal. Excluding stale or junk data reduces storage, effort, and risk.

questions.q: Where should a trial load be run before production?
options: Directly in production with a small batch
On a colleague's laptop with a different tool
Nowhere; trial loads are not useful
In a sandbox, so surprises happen where they are cheap to fix
questions.explain: Rehearsing in a sandbox exposes mapping, validation, and automation problems before production data is touched.

questions.q: Which setting must an org enable if a migration needs to preserve original created dates?
options: Enable Duplicate Rules
Set Audit Fields upon Record Creation
Restrict Picklist Values
Enable Bulk API 3.0
questions.explain: Writing values such as CreatedDate on insert requires the Set Audit Fields upon Record Creation setting (and matching permission), so plan for it early.

questions.q: Which item belongs in a one-page migration plan?
options: Only the CSV file names
Only the login credentials for each user
Load order, field mapping, excluded data with reasons, External Id fields, automation to pause, and a validation plan
Only the date of the go-live party
questions.explain: A migration plan documents scope, order, mapping, keys, automation handling, and validation, so everything is decided in advance.
